## Results {#sec-results}

### Retrieval Performance

We evaluate Memory Palace against standard RAG systems on retrieval accuracy and context efficiency.

![Retrieval accuracy and context size comparison across methods](figures/retrieval_comparison.png){#fig-retrieval-comparison}

| Method | Recall@1 | Recall@3 | MRR | Context (KB) | Latency (ms) |
|--------|----------|----------|-----|--------------|--------------|
| Flat RAG | 72% | 84% | 0.77 | 46.5 | 245 |
| HyDE | 75% | 86% | 0.79 | 52.3 | 312 |
| RAPTOR | 78% | 88% | 0.82 | 38.2 | 287 |
| GraphRAG | 81% | 91% | 0.85 | 41.7 | 356 |
| **Memory Palace** | **89%** | **96%** | **0.92** | **1.2** | **89** |

: LLM Retrieval Performance Comparison {#tbl-retrieval}

**Key Finding (RQ1)**: Memory Palace achieves **89% Recall@1** compared to GraphRAG's 81%, while using **97% less context** (1.2KB vs 46.5KB). The 2-hop hierarchical index routes queries to domain-specific partitions, reducing search space and improving precision.

### Context Scaling

![Context size scaling: flat RAG vs hierarchical retrieval](figures/context_scaling.png){#fig-context-scaling}

At scale, the context efficiency advantage becomes dramatic:

| Corpus Size | Flat RAG | Memory Palace | Reduction |
|-------------|----------|---------------|-----------|
| 100 memories | 50 KB | 1.2 KB | 97.6% |
| 500 memories | 250 KB | 2.0 KB | 99.2% |
| 1,000 memories | 500 KB | 2.5 KB | 99.5% |

**Key Finding (RQ3)**: Hierarchical retrieval maintains near-constant context size regardless of corpus size, enabling Memory Palace to scale to large knowledge bases without exhausting LLM context windows.

### Hallucination Detection

![Hallucination detection: accuracy vs compute cost](figures/hallucination_detection.png){#fig-hallucination}

| Method | Precision | Recall | F1 | Compute Cost |
|--------|-----------|--------|-----|--------------|
| Standard RAG | 62% | 58% | 60% | 1× |
| SelfCheckGPT | 78% | 72% | 75% | 5× |
| RefChecker | 81% | 75% | 78% | 3× |
| FActScore | 85% | 81% | 83% | 6× |
| **MP Verify Tokens** | **94%** | **91%** | **92%** | **0.01×** |

: Hallucination Detection Comparison {#tbl-hallucination}

**Key Finding (RQ2)**: Verification tokens achieve **F1=0.92** for hallucination detection—11% higher than FActScore while being **600× cheaper** computationally. Detection requires only a string match, not additional LLM inference.

### SOTA System Comparison

![NDCG@10 comparison with SOTA embedding and retrieval systems](figures/sota_comparison.png){#fig-sota}

We compare against published results from leading embedding and retrieval systems:

| System | NDCG@10 | Parameters | Context Limit |
|--------|---------|------------|---------------|
| Google Gecko | 66.3% | 1.2B | 2,048 |
| Cohere embed-v4 | 65.2% | ~1B | 512 |
| OpenAI text-embedding-3-large | 64.6% | Unknown | 8,191 |
| ColBERT | 52.4% | 110M | 512 |
| **Memory Palace** | **58.2%** | **0** | **Unlimited** |

: SOTA Embedding System Comparison {#tbl-sota}

While Memory Palace scores lower on raw NDCG than commercial embedding systems, it requires **zero parameters** and has **no context window limits**—enabling deployment without API costs or embedding infrastructure.

### BEIR Benchmark Results

![BEIR benchmark comparison across datasets](figures/beir_comparison.png){#fig-beir}

| Method | Natural Questions | HotpotQA | MS MARCO | Average |
|--------|-------------------|----------|----------|---------|
| BM25 | 32.9% | 60.3% | 22.8% | 38.7% |
| Contriever | 49.8% | 63.8% | 40.7% | 51.4% |
| ColBERT | 52.4% | 59.3% | 40.0% | 50.6% |
| GraphRAG | 55.7% | 64.3% | 41.2% | 53.7% |
| **Memory Palace** | **58.2%** | **67.1%** | **42.8%** | **56.0%** |

: BEIR Zero-Shot Retrieval Results {#tbl-beir}

**Key Finding (RQ4)**: Memory Palace achieves **4.3% higher average NDCG** than GraphRAG while using 97% less context. The hierarchical domain routing particularly excels on multi-hop reasoning datasets like HotpotQA (+2.8% over GraphRAG).
